page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized, Graviton-based instance powered by 32 dedicated physical ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 64 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per physical core memory allocation. Local storage is provided via 1900 GB of NVMe SSD instance store, combined with a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Hardware-accelerated AES cryptography is supported, though x86-specific vector extensions like AVX are absent due to the arm64 architecture.

In synthetic and practical benchmarks, the c6gd.8xlarge demonstrates solid parallel processing efficiency alongside single-threaded performance constraints. Multi-core performance is average across key metrics, achieving 48,571.1 on stress-ng multi-core and 11,706.0 on Geekbench multi-core. However, single-core execution shows lower relative output, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and weak single-threaded gzip compression throughput at 20.31 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth reaches 173.34 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

The combination of dedicated arm64 physical cores and 1900 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage provides strong resource density for IO-intensive distributed computing. Redis throughput reaches 40.61 million SET operations per second, and PassMark database operations benchmark at 20,441.91. Static web serving throughput measures 33.11 GB/sec. These specifications make the instance best suited for web serving, database clusters, containerized applications, and multi-threaded batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized arm64 instance featuring 32 physical AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 cores running at 2.5 GHz with 64 GB of memory and 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server offers 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and hardware AES encryption support. Multi-core compute benchmarks report steady performance, with stress-ng reaching 48,571.1 and Geekbench multi-core scoring 11,706.0. High-speed local NVMe storage enables solid data throughput, yielding 40.61 million SET operations per second in Redis tests and 33.11 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. However, single-core workloads experience throughput constraints, as seen in lower single-threaded compression scores. The instance provides an efficient ratio of physical core density and direct-attached NVMe storage, making it well suited for web serving, distributed database nodes, containerized microservices, and multi-threaded batch processing workloads.
